[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC3, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14926 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 7 MW of critical IT load and 55,780 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC3 sits on the Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, and publishes 7 MW of IT capacity across 55,780 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 7 MW supports roughly 700 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same load supports roughly 175 racks. Those are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. The published floor area works out to about 8 square feet per kilowatt at the 10 kW assumption, which is consistent with a mixed-use colocation design rather than a purpose-built high-density AI training shell.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no statement can be made about which compliance regimes the campus qualifies for. Connectivity specifications and redundancy tier ratings are also not published on the operator page this site has read.

Among the 21 data center facilities mapped in Utah, only 3 publish a megawatt figure, and those 3 together account for 39 MW of known IT capacity. SLC3's 7 MW places it third among those three facilities, representing roughly 18 percent of the published total. Because most mapped Utah facilities publish no capacity figure, the true installed base in the state is larger than 39 MW, and this campus's actual share is smaller than that number implies. For an AI workload planner, 7 MW is a modest footprint, sufficient for inference or smaller training runs but well below the scale of purpose-built hyperscale campuses that now anchor large model training programs.
